American Crocodile Scute Mercury Analyses

Kylie

2026-09-02

============================================================

American Crocodile Scute Mercury Analyses

============================================================

Analyses:

1. Hg concentration and body size (SVL)

2. Hatchling clutch and nest-site effects

3. Juvenile sex effects

4. Hatchling vs. juvenile Hg concentrations

5. Publication figures and summary outputs

Multiple scute subsamples from the same crocodile are averaged

to obtain one individual-level THg concentration before all

biological analyses. Because scute material could not be

homogenized, these are treated as spatial subsamples rather

than scute subsamples of a homogenized sample.

============================================================

————————————————————

1. PACKAGES

————————————————————

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(performance)
library(patchwork)
library(forcats)
library(clubSandwich)
library(here)
library(see)

————————————————————

2. IMPORT AND PREPARE DATA

————————————————————

Multiple scute subsamples from the same crocodile were averaged to obtain one individual-level THg concentration. Because scute material could not be homogenized, these measurements were treated as spatial subsamples rather than technical replicates of a homogenized sample.

Import Raw Data

raw <- read_xlsx(
  here("American_Crocodile_Mercury_Data.xlsx")
)

————————————————————

Summarize scute subsamples within each crocodile

————————————————————

Scute material could not be homogenized before analysis.

Repeated measurements from the same crocodile are therefore

treated as spatial scute subsamples rather than conventional

scute subsamples of a homogeneous tissue sample.

The mean across available scute subsamples is used as the

individual-level THg concentration for the PRIMARY analyses.

Within-individual CV is calculated for quality assessment and

for a separate sensitivity analysis using a 15% cutoff.

————————————————————

dat <- raw %>%
  group_by(`Scute ID`) %>%
  summarise(
    n_subsamples = sum(!is.na(`CONC [ug/kg]`)),
    Hg_ugkg = mean(`CONC [ug/kg]`, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Hg_ugkg = ifelse(
      n_subsamples > 1,
      sd(`CONC [ug/kg]`, na.rm = TRUE),
      NA_real_
    ),
    CV_percent = ifelse(
      n_subsamples > 1,
      (SD_Hg_ugkg / Hg_ugkg) * 100,
      NA_real_
    ),
    TL = first(`TL (cm)`),
    SizeClass = first(`Size Class`),
    SVL = first(`SVL (cm)`),
    Weight = first(`Weight (g)`),
    Sex = first(Sex),
    Clutch = first(Clutch),
    Site = first(`Nest Location`),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
     # Convert µg/kg to µg/g
    Hg_ugg = Hg_ugkg / 1000,
    SD_Hg_ugg = SD_Hg_ugkg / 1000,

    # Sensitivity-analysis flag.
    # Animals represented by one scute subsample are retained
    # because within-individual CV cannot be calculated.
    CV15_status = case_when(
      n_subsamples == 1 ~ "Single subsample - retained",
      CV_percent <= 15 ~ "CV <=15% - retained",
      CV_percent > 15 ~ "CV >15% - excluded in sensitivity analysis",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    CV15_include = n_subsamples == 1 | CV_percent <= 15,

    SizeClass = factor(
      SizeClass,
      levels = c("Hatchling", "Juvenile", "Subadult")
    ),

    Sex = factor(Sex),
    Clutch_f = factor(Clutch),
    Site = factor(Site),

    # Transformations used in statistical models
    logHg = log10(Hg_ugg),
    logSVL = log10(SVL)
  )

Inspect within-individual scute variability

dat %>%
  select(
    `Scute ID`, SizeClass, n_subsamples,
    Hg_ugg, SD_Hg_ugg, CV_percent, CV15_status
  ) %>%

Age-class datasets

hatchlings <- dat %>%
  filter(SizeClass == "Hatchling") %>%
  mutate(
    logSVL_c = logSVL - mean(logSVL, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

juveniles <- dat %>%
  filter(SizeClass == "Juvenile") %>%
  mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("F", "M")),
    logSVL_c = logSVL - mean(logSVL, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

Confirm sample sizes

table(dat$SizeClass)
## 
## Hatchling  Juvenile  Subadult 
##        49        22         1
table(juveniles$Sex)
## 
##  F  M 
##  7 15

============================================================

ANALYSIS 1. BODY SIZE AND SCUTE Hg

============================================================

————————————————————

1A. All individuals

————————————————————

Analysis 1. Body Size and Scute THg

1A. All Individuals

mod_SVL_all <- lm(
  logHg ~ logSVL,
  data = dat
)

summary(mod_SVL_all)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = logHg ~ logSVL, data = dat)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -0.218613 -0.070707 -0.000642  0.060552  0.271998 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) -2.44955    0.11223  -21.83   <2e-16 ***
## logSVL       1.40595    0.09433   14.90   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.1163 on 70 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.7604, Adjusted R-squared:  0.757 
## F-statistic: 222.2 on 1 and 70 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
confint(mod_SVL_all)
##                 2.5 %    97.5 %
## (Intercept) -2.673377 -2.225717
## logSVL       1.217820  1.594085
performance::r2(mod_SVL_all)
## # R2 for Linear Regression
##        R2: 0.760
##   adj. R2: 0.757
performance::check_model(mod_SVL_all)

1C. Hatchlings

mod_SVL_hatchling <- lmer(
  logHg ~ logSVL_c + (1 | Clutch_f),
  data = hatchlings,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(mod_SVL_hatchling)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method ['lmerModLmerTest']
## Formula: logHg ~ logSVL_c + (1 | Clutch_f)
##    Data: hatchlings
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: -88.9
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -1.87657 -0.56061  0.00647  0.66883  2.03468 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Clutch_f (Intercept) 0.005407 0.07353 
##  Residual             0.007076 0.08412 
## Number of obs: 49, groups:  Clutch_f, 8
## 
## Fixed effects:
##             Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  -0.9048     0.0300  5.1219 -30.159 5.76e-07 ***
## logSVL_c      0.6357     0.7896 45.9976   0.805    0.425    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##          (Intr)
## logSVL_c -0.121
anova(mod_SVL_hatchling)
## Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
##             Sum Sq   Mean Sq NumDF  DenDF F value Pr(>F)
## logSVL_c 0.0045857 0.0045857     1 45.998  0.6481 0.4249
confint(mod_SVL_hatchling, method = "Wald")
##                  2.5 %     97.5 %
## .sig01              NA         NA
## .sigma              NA         NA
## (Intercept) -0.9635689 -0.8459697
## logSVL_c    -0.9119771  2.1833849
performance::r2(mod_SVL_hatchling)
## # R2 for Mixed Models
## 
##   Conditional R2: 0.439
##      Marginal R2: 0.010
performance::check_model(mod_SVL_hatchling)

Fixed-effect predictions for hatchling figure

SVL_seq <- seq(
  min(hatchlings$logSVL_c, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(hatchlings$logSVL_c, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 200
)

pred_hatch <- emmeans(
  mod_SVL_hatchling,
  ~ logSVL_c,
  at = list(logSVL_c = SVL_seq)
) %>%
  as.data.frame()

pred_hatch$logSVL <- pred_hatch$logSVL_c +
  mean(hatchlings$logSVL, na.rm = TRUE)

2B. Variance attributable to clutch

mod_clutch <- lmer(
  logHg ~ 1 + (1 | Clutch_f),
  data = hatchlings,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(mod_clutch)

##

## Scaled residuals:

icc_clutch <- performance::icc(

Estimated marginal means by site

site_emm <- emmeans(
  mod_site_clutch,
  ~ Site
)

site_emm
##  Site                        emmean     SE   df lower.CL upper.CL
##  Isla Cabritos (Playita)     -0.938 0.0327 3.03   -1.042   -0.835
##  Isla Cabritos (Punte Oeste) -0.778 0.0473 3.82   -0.911   -0.644
##  KM 5                        -0.922 0.0558 2.39   -1.129   -0.716
##  Las Azufradas (La Charca)   -0.983 0.0591 3.00   -1.171   -0.795
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95
pairs(site_emm, adjust = "tukey")
##  contrast                                                estimate     SE   df t.ratio
##  Isla Cabritos (Playita) - Isla Cabritos (Punte Oeste)    -0.1605 0.0576 3.54  -2.789
##  Isla Cabritos (Playita) - KM 5                           -0.0157 0.0647 2.52  -0.242
##  Isla Cabritos (Playita) - Las Azufradas (La Charca)       0.0452 0.0675 3.01   0.669
##  Isla Cabritos (Punte Oeste) - KM 5                        0.1449 0.0732 2.85   1.979
##  Isla Cabritos (Punte Oeste) - Las Azufradas (La Charca)   0.2057 0.0757 3.28   2.718
##  KM 5 - Las Azufradas (La Charca)                          0.0609 0.0812 2.69   0.749
##  p.value
##   0.1659
##   0.9938
##   0.9026
##   0.3657
##   0.1866
##   0.8723
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 4 estimates
site_results <- as.data.frame(
  confint(site_emm)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Hg_ugg = 10^emmean,
    lower_Hg = 10^lower.CL,
    upper_Hg = 10^upper.CL
  )

============================================================

ANALYSIS 3. JUVENILE SEX EFFECTS

============================================================

————————————————————

3A. Does body size differ by sex?

————————————————————

juvenile_sex_summary <- juveniles %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_SVL = mean(SVL, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_SVL = sd(SVL, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_SVL = median(SVL, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_SVL = min(SVL, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_SVL = max(SVL, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

juvenile_sex_summary
## # A tibble: 2 × 7
##   Sex       n mean_SVL SD_SVL median_SVL min_SVL max_SVL
##   <fct> <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1 F         7     26.4  11.3        18.2    16.5    40.9
## 2 M        15     20.4   6.86       17.9    17.1    38
sex_SVL_test <- t.test(
  SVL ~ Sex,
  data = juveniles
)

sex_SVL_test
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  SVL by Sex
## t = 1.3047, df = 8.1547, p-value = 0.2276
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group F and group M is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -4.581809 16.612285
## sample estimates:
## mean in group F mean in group M 
##        26.42857        20.41333

————————————————————

3B. Does the Hg-SVL relationship differ by sex?

————————————————————

mod_sex_interaction <- lm(
  logHg ~ logSVL_c * Sex,
  data = juveniles
)

summary(mod_sex_interaction)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = logHg ~ logSVL_c * Sex, data = juveniles)
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -0.21279 -0.08091 -0.00917  0.09251  0.15754 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)   -0.58370    0.04602 -12.683 2.06e-10 ***
## logSVL_c       1.01843    0.25305   4.025 0.000795 ***
## SexM           0.04921    0.05520   0.892 0.384394    
## logSVL_c:SexM -0.29792    0.36859  -0.808 0.429495    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.1138 on 18 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.5711, Adjusted R-squared:  0.4996 
## F-statistic:  7.99 on 3 and 18 DF,  p-value: 0.001355
anova(mod_sex_interaction)
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Response: logHg
##              Df   Sum Sq  Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)

sex_slopes <- emtrends(

ANALYSIS 4. HATCHLING VS. JUVENILE Hg

============================================================

Subadult excluded from this two-group comparison

sizeclass_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(SizeClass %in% c("Hatchling", "Juvenile")) %>%
  droplevels()

————————————————————

4A. Descriptive statistics

————————————————————

sizeclass_summary <- sizeclass_dat %>%
  group_by(SizeClass) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_Hg = mean(Hg_ugg, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Hg = sd(Hg_ugg, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_Hg = median(Hg_ugg, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_Hg = min(Hg_ugg, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_Hg = max(Hg_ugg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sizeclass_summary
## # A tibble: 2 × 7
##   SizeClass     n mean_Hg  SD_Hg median_Hg min_Hg max_Hg
##   <fct>     <int>   <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 Hatchling    49   0.125 0.0312     0.123 0.0774  0.242
## 2 Juvenile     22   0.306 0.122      0.251 0.164   0.633

————————————————————

4B. Welch’s t-test on log-transformed Hg

————————————————————

sizeclass_test <- t.test(
  logHg ~ SizeClass,
  data = sizeclass_dat
)

sizeclass_test
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  logHg by SizeClass
## t = -9.9696, df = 29.319, p-value = 6.289e-11
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Hatchling and group Juvenile is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.4497010 -0.2966593
## sample estimates:
## mean in group Hatchling  mean in group Juvenile 
##              -0.9171895              -0.5440093

————————————————————

4C. Geometric means and group-specific 95% CI

————————————————————

sizeclass_geo <- sizeclass_dat %>%
  group_by(SizeClass) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_log = mean(logHg, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_log = sd(logHg, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_log = sd_log / sqrt(n),
    tcrit = qt(0.975, df = n - 1),
    
    geometric_mean = 10^mean_log,
    
    lower_CI = 10^(mean_log - tcrit * SE_log),
    upper_CI = 10^(mean_log + tcrit * SE_log),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sizeclass_geo
## # A tibble: 2 × 9
##   SizeClass     n mean_log sd_log SE_log tcrit geometric_mean lower_CI upper_CI
##   <fct>     <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>          <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 Hatchling    49   -0.917  0.105 0.0150  2.01          0.121    0.113    0.130
## 2 Juvenile     22   -0.544  0.161 0.0343  2.08          0.286    0.242    0.337

Juvenile:Hatchling geometric-mean ratio

Welch output is Hatchling - Juvenile, so signs are reversed.

log_ratio <- -diff(sizeclass_test$estimate)

Difference in geometric means on the log10 scale

log_difference <- (
  mean(sizeclass_dat$logHg[sizeclass_dat$SizeClass == "Juvenile"]) -
    mean(sizeclass_dat$logHg[sizeclass_dat$SizeClass == "Hatchling"])
)

Back-transform to obtain juvenile:hatchling ratio

fold_difference <- 10^log_difference

fold_difference
## [1] 2.361458
fold_CI <- 10^c(
  -sizeclass_test$conf.int[2],
  -sizeclass_test$conf.int[1]
)

cat(
  "\nJuvenile:Hatchling geometric mean ratio =",
  round(fold_difference, 2),
  "\n95% CI =",
  round(fold_CI[1], 2), "to",
  round(fold_CI[2], 2),
  "\n"
)
## 
## Juvenile:Hatchling geometric mean ratio = 2.36 
## 95% CI = 1.98 to 2.82

============================================================

ANALYSIS 4D. CLUSTER-AWARE HATCHLING VS. JUVENILE COMPARISON

============================================================

Hatchlings from the same clutch are not fully independent.

This analysis uses CR2 cluster-robust standard errors, with

clutch defining the cluster for hatchlings and each juvenile

treated as an independent cluster.

Requires: clubSandwich (loaded with other packages above)

============================================================

————————————————————

Create cluster IDs

————————————————————

sizeclass_cluster <- sizeclass_dat %>%
  mutate(
    cluster_id = if_else(
      SizeClass == "Hatchling",
      paste0("H_", Clutch),
      paste0("J_", `Scute ID`)
    )
  )

Check cluster structure

sizeclass_cluster %>%
  count(SizeClass, cluster_id)
## # A tibble: 30 × 3
##    SizeClass cluster_id     n
##    <fct>     <chr>      <int>
##  1 Hatchling H_1            1
##  2 Hatchling H_3           10
##  3 Hatchling H_4            4
##  4 Hatchling H_5           10
##  5 Hatchling H_6            6
##  6 Hatchling H_7            9
##  7 Hatchling H_8            7
##  8 Hatchling H_9            2
##  9 Juvenile  J_178          1
## 10 Juvenile  J_179          1
## # ℹ 20 more rows

————————————————————

Fit size-class model

————————————————————

mod_sizeclass_cluster <- lm(
  logHg ~ SizeClass,
  data = sizeclass_cluster
)

————————————————————

CR2 cluster-robust inference

————————————————————

cluster_test <- coef_test(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = sizeclass_cluster$cluster_id,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)

cluster_test
## Alternative hypothesis: two-sided 
##              Coef. Estimate     SE Null value t-stat d.f. (Satt) p-val (Satt) Sig.
##        (Intercept)   -0.917 0.0266          0  -34.5        5.22       <0.001  ***
##  SizeClassJuvenile    0.373 0.0434          0    8.6       24.34       <0.001  ***

Cluster-robust 95% confidence intervals

cluster_CI <- conf_int(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = sizeclass_cluster$cluster_id,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)

cluster_CI
##              Coef. Estimate     SE  d.f. Lower 95% CI Upper 95% CI
##        (Intercept)   -0.917 0.0266  5.22       -0.985       -0.850
##  SizeClassJuvenile    0.373 0.0434 24.34        0.284        0.463

————————————————————

Back-transform juvenile:hatchling effect

————————————————————

Hatchling is the reference group, so the Juvenile coefficient

represents log10(Juvenile Hg) - log10(Hatchling Hg).

beta_stage <- coef(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster
)["SizeClassJuvenile"]

fold_cluster <- 10^beta_stage

fold_cluster
## SizeClassJuvenile 
##          2.361458

ANALYSIS 4E. CLUTCH-LEVEL SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS

Compare hatchling clutch means with juvenile individuals

============================================================

This provides a simple complementary analysis in which each

hatchling clutch contributes one independent observation.

============================================================

hatch_clutch_means <- hatchlings %>%
  group_by(Clutch_f) %>%
  summarise(
    logHg = mean(logHg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    SizeClass = "Hatchling"
  )

juvenile_individuals <- juveniles %>%
  transmute(
    logHg,
    SizeClass = "Juvenile"
  )

sizeclass_sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  hatch_clutch_means,
  juvenile_individuals
) %>%
  mutate(
    SizeClass = factor(
      SizeClass,
      levels = c("Hatchling", "Juvenile")
    )
  )

sizeclass_sensitivity_test <- t.test(
  logHg ~ SizeClass,
  data = sizeclass_sensitivity
)

sizeclass_sensitivity_test
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  logHg by SizeClass
## t = -7.2929, df = 21.153, p-value = 3.362e-07
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Hatchling and group Juvenile is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.4529455 -0.2520102
## sample estimates:
## mean in group Hatchling  mean in group Juvenile 
##              -0.8964872              -0.5440093

============================================================

ANALYSIS 5. SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS USING WITHIN-INDIVIDUAL

SCUTE-SUBSAMPLE CV <= 15%

============================================================

PURPOSE:

Determine whether the primary biological conclusions change

when individuals with >15% variability among multiple scute

subsamples are excluded.

IMPORTANT:

- This does NOT replace the primary analysis.

- Animals represented by one scute subsample are retained,

because a within-individual CV cannot be calculated.

- Centering and derived datasets are recreated after filtering.

============================================================

————————————————————

5A. Create CV-restricted individual-level dataset

————————————————————

dat_CV15 <- dat %>%
  filter(CV15_include) %>%
  droplevels()

hatchlings_CV15 <- dat_CV15 %>%
  filter(SizeClass == "Hatchling") %>%
  mutate(
    Clutch_f = factor(Clutch),
    Site = factor(Site),
    logSVL_c = logSVL - mean(logSVL, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

juveniles_CV15 <- dat_CV15 %>%
  filter(SizeClass == "Juvenile") %>%
  mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("F", "M")),
    logSVL_c = logSVL - mean(logSVL, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

CV15_n_comparison <- bind_rows(
  dat %>%
    count(SizeClass, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(dataset = "Primary - all individuals"),
  dat_CV15 %>%
    count(SizeClass, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(dataset = "Sensitivity - CV <=15% or single subsample")
) %>%
  select(dataset, SizeClass, n)

CV15_n_comparison
## # A tibble: 6 × 3
##   dataset                                    SizeClass     n
##   <chr>                                      <fct>     <int>
## 1 Primary - all individuals                  Hatchling    49
## 2 Primary - all individuals                  Juvenile     22
## 3 Primary - all individuals                  Subadult      1
## 4 Sensitivity - CV <=15% or single subsample Hatchling    33
## 5 Sensitivity - CV <=15% or single subsample Juvenile     18
## 6 Sensitivity - CV <=15% or single subsample Subadult      1

————————————————————

mod_SVL_all_CV15 <- lm(
  logHg ~ logSVL,

)

summary(mod_SVL_all_CV15)

    .groups = "drop"

juvenile_sex_summary_CV15
## # A tibble: 2 × 7

sex_SVL_test_CV15 <- t.test(
  SVL ~ Sex,
  data = juveniles_CV15
)

sex_SVL_test_CV15
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  SVL by Sex
## t = 1.442, df = 8.2628, p-value = 0.1861
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group F and group M is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -3.945582 17.311815
## sample estimates:
## mean in group F mean in group M 
##        26.42857        19.74545
mod_sex_interaction_CV15 <- lm(
  logHg ~ logSVL_c * Sex,
  data = juveniles_CV15
)

summary(mod_sex_interaction_CV15)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = logHg ~ logSVL_c * Sex, data = juveniles_CV15)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -0.219292 -0.078087  0.005463  0.084158  0.144851 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)   -0.58350    0.04906 -11.894 1.05e-08 ***
## logSVL_c       1.01843    0.26984   3.774  0.00205 ** 
## SexM           0.03799    0.06322   0.601  0.55751    
## logSVL_c:SexM -0.62305    0.47081  -1.323  0.20693    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.1214 on 14 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.5311, Adjusted R-squared:  0.4306 
## F-statistic: 5.285 on 3 and 14 DF,  p-value: 0.01202
anova(mod_sex_interaction_CV15)
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Response: logHg
##              Df   Sum Sq  Mean Sq F value   Pr(>F)   
## logSVL_c      1 0.201207 0.201207 13.6629 0.002395 **
## Sex           1 0.006503 0.006503  0.4416 0.517168   
## logSVL_c:Sex  1 0.025790 0.025790  1.7513 0.206925   
## Residuals    14 0.206172 0.014727                    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
sex_slopes_CV15 <- emtrends(
  mod_sex_interaction_CV15,
  ~ Sex,
  var = "logSVL_c"
)

sex_slopes_CV15
##  Sex logSVL_c.trend    SE df lower.CL upper.CL

##

pairs(sex_slopes_CV15)

5H. Hatchling vs juvenile age-class comparison:

CR2 cluster-robust inference

————————————————————

sizeclass_CV15 <- dat_CV15 %>%
  filter(SizeClass %in% c("Hatchling", "Juvenile")) %>%
  droplevels() %>%
  mutate(
    SizeClass = factor(
      SizeClass,
      levels = c("Hatchling", "Juvenile")
    ),
    cluster_id = if_else(
      SizeClass == "Hatchling",
      paste0("H_", Clutch),
      paste0("J_", `Scute ID`)
    )
  )

mod_sizeclass_cluster_CV15 <- lm(
  logHg ~ SizeClass,
  data = sizeclass_CV15
)

cluster_test_CV15 <- coef_test(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster_CV15,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = sizeclass_CV15$cluster_id,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)

cluster_test_CV15
## Alternative hypothesis: two-sided 
##              Coef. Estimate     SE Null value t-stat d.f. (Satt) p-val (Satt) Sig.
##        (Intercept)   -0.924 0.0255          0  -36.3        4.28       <0.001  ***
##  SizeClassJuvenile    0.379 0.0457          0    8.3       18.60       <0.001  ***
cluster_CI_CV15 <- conf_int(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster_CV15,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = sizeclass_CV15$cluster_id,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)

cluster_CI_CV15
##              Coef. Estimate     SE  d.f. Lower 95% CI Upper 95% CI
##        (Intercept)   -0.924 0.0255  4.28       -0.993       -0.855
##  SizeClassJuvenile    0.379 0.0457 18.60        0.283        0.475
beta_stage_CV15 <- coef(
  mod_sizeclass_cluster_CV15
)["SizeClassJuvenile"]

fold_cluster_CV15 <- 10^beta_stage_CV15

fold_cluster_CV15
## SizeClassJuvenile 
##          2.394056

Unique clutch colors used only in Panel A

Chosen to be distinct from the site palette in Panel B

————————————————————

clutch_colors <- c(
  "1" = "#332288",
  "3" = "#88CCEE",
  "4" = "#44AA99",
  "5" = "#117733",
  "6" = "#999933",
  "7" = "#DDCC77",
  "8" = "#AA4499",
  "9" = "#882255"
)

============================================================

Panel A: Hatchling THg by clutch

Color + shape both identify clutch

============================================================

p3A <- ggplot(
  hatchlings_plot,
  aes(
    x = Clutch_f,
    y = Hg_ugg,
    fill = Clutch_f,
    color = Clutch_f,
    shape = Clutch_f
  )
) +
  
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.60,
    alpha = 0.30,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.10,
    height = 0,
    size = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = clutch_colors
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = clutch_colors
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = clutch_shapes
  ) +
  
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = Inf,
    y = Inf,
    label = "ICC = 0.479",
    hjust = 1.10,
    vjust = 1.30,
    size = 4
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Clutch-Level Variation",
    x = "Clutch",
    y = expression("Scute THg (" * mu * "g/g)")
  ) +
  
  guides(
    fill = "none",
    color = "none",
    shape = "none"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)

============================================================

Panel B: Hatchling THg by nest site and clutch

Color = nest site

Shape = clutch

============================================================

p3B <- ggplot(
  hatchlings_plot,
  aes(
    x = Site_short,
    y = Hg_ugg,
    fill = Site_short
  )
) +
  
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.60,
    alpha = 0.35,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  
  geom_jitter(
    aes(
      color = Site_short,
      shape = Clutch_f
    ),
    width = 0.13,
    height = 0,
    size = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.90
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = site_colors
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = site_colors
  ) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = clutch_shapes
  ) +
  
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = Inf,
    y = Inf,
    label = "Site: p = 0.151",
    hjust = 1.10,
    vjust = 1.30,
    size = 4
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Nest Site and Clutch",
    x = "Nest site",
    y = expression("Scute THg (" * mu * "g/g)"),
    shape = "Clutch"
  ) +
  
  guides(
    fill = "none",
    color = "none",
    shape = guide_legend(
      title = "Clutch",
      override.aes = list(
        color = "black",
        size = 3.5,
        alpha = 1
      )
    )
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 25,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

============================================================

Combine Figure 3

============================================================

figure3 <- p3A + p3B +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A",
    title = "Clutch and Nest-Site Variation in Hatchling Scute Mercury"
  ) &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 14
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

figure3
